update.installFailedTitle: That update could not be installed
update.failedChecksum: The download did not match the checksum the release published, so it was deleted and nothing was run. This is almost always a download that went wrong — try again, or get the installer from the release page.
update.failedNoAsset: This release has no installer this app can verify, so there is nothing to install automatically. The release page has the files.
update.failedNoOffer: That release is no longer on offer — it was withdrawn, replaced, or could not be confirmed since this box opened. Nothing was downloaded. Check for updates again to see what's available now.
update.failedUnsupported: One-click updates are Windows-only for now. The release page has what you need.
update.failedNoToken: This machine has no credentials for the release files, so the download could not start.
update.failedAuth: The credentials on this machine were refused when downloading the installer.
update.failedDisk: The installer could not be written to this machine's temporary folder.
update.failedLaunch: The installer downloaded and verified, but Windows would not start it.
update.failedNetwork: The download did not finish. Nothing was installed and nothing was left behind.

workspace.readOnlyTitle: Nothing in this workspace will be saved.
workspace.readOnlyBody: Its file was written by a newer version of switchboard.ai, and saving it from this one would throw away whatever that version added — so the file is being left untouched. Everything here works normally, but nothing you change this run — sessions, layout, groups, settings — will be there next launch. Run the newer version of switchboard.ai again to save as normal.
workspace.saveFailedBody: switchboard.ai keeps failing to write {file} — usually a drive with no room left, a permission on that folder, or another program (a backup or anti-virus tool) holding the file open. Everything here works normally, and nothing on screen is lost, but changes since the last save that worked — sessions, layout, groups, settings — won't be there next launch. Check that drive for free space and close anything that might have the file open; switchboard.ai keeps trying, and this notice goes away by itself the moment a save works.

push.title: Phone push & webhooks
push.intro: Have a session reach you when you are away from the machine, or tell another program about it. Both are off until you set one up, and neither can hold a session up.
push.unavailable: This machine has no credential store available, so nothing can be saved here. On Linux that usually means no keyring (gnome-keyring or kwallet) is running.
push.ntfyTopicHint: Any name you like, but pick an unguessable one: anyone who knows it can read your notifications. Subscribe to the same topic in the ntfy app on your phone.
push.ntfyServerHint: Leave empty for ntfy.sh. Set it if you run your own ntfy.
push.webhookUrlHint: Every event is POSTed here as JSON. Treated as a secret, because webhook URLs usually are.
push.enablePushHint: Needs permission, needs input, and crashes — only while you are away from switchboard.
push.enableWebhookHint: All four events, whatever the window is doing: a program is not distracted by being looked at. The 🔔 switch and quiet hours still silence it.

reason.no-store: this machine has no credential store.
reason.bad-url: that address is not a usable http(s) URL.
reason.refused: the service turned it down — check the details you pasted.

problem.bad-url: Not saved — that needs to be a full http(s) address, like https://example.com/hook.
problem.url-userinfo: Not saved — a server address is kept in plain text, so it may not carry a username or password.
problem.not-stored: Not saved — this machine's credential store would not take it.

push.secretNote: Saved in your operating system's credential store, never in a switchboard file.
